why:
Measured against the recorded upstream surfaces (`docs/reference/api-surface/{rclc,rclcpp,rclrs}.json`): none of them contains `park`, `wake_source`, `spin_nominal` or `granularity` at all, so there is no upstream name to align to. Same basis as the `Executor::release_jitter` pair beside it.

phase-436, re-exported by B2. `unsafe extern "C" fn(ctx) -> u64` — microseconds from now, `u64::MAX` for "nothing pending". A fn POINTER rather than a closure is the `no_std`/no-allocator constraint, the same one behind the pubsub stage's callback rows, and `extern "C"` is what lets a C port and a Rust port contribute through one slot. The first real one is smoltcp's `poll_delay` (B2). rclrs's executor waits on a wait set and has no notion of a source DECLARING when it will next need servicing. NOTE this is a SCHEDULING deadline, not the QoS policy of the same name — see `c:deadline_policy_t` for the same collision one language over. (Shard: `topics.py` routes this key to this file rather than to exec/, where its `Executor::register_wake_source` / `Executor::last_park` siblings live — the same split `c:deadline_policy_t` records. The verdict is right; the shard is an artifact of the key's wording.)
